meaning: This makes the external port flow the negative of the vessel volume rate, fixing the sign convention by which flow through `ext` inflates or deflates the compartment. Together with line 253 it forces D(V) = C*D(Ptm).

could_move.what: Sign convention on ext.q sets the direction of volume exchange; flipping it inverts the volume response to the same external flow
Lines 247 and 253 both define ext.q, so they act as one structural constraint linking D(V) and D(Ptm); this changes which variables survive as states after structural simplification
A ~ V/(N_v*l_v) propagates any change in V to cross-sectional area, and from there to terms that use A
C ~ 1/(k_v*(Ptm - p0_v)) is singular at Ptm = p0_v, so this coupling can become stiff or fail near that pressure
The only entry point found is main.jl, so effects appear in whatever that script solves and plots

expectation: Unknown from this context. A wrong sign would send volume and pressure the opposite way; an inconsistency between lines 247 and 253 would instead make the system over- or under-determined. I cannot tell which from the excerpt.

check.why: Runs the one known entry point end to end, cheaper than a re-fit. It surfaces structural-simplification errors from the two definitions of ext.q and shows the sign of the volume and pressure traces.
